title: Oscar Romero
hookLine: an archbishop in El Salvador speaks for the poor and is shot while saying Mass

lines: SOME EXPECTED HIM TO KEEP QUIET.
cards: A list of names, read aloud from the pulpit of the cathedral in San Salvador on a Sunday morning. First the archbishop has read the gospel and explained it. Now he reads the week's news.
People taken from their homes. People found dead by the road. Priests, farmers, students.
Across the country, in shops and farmhouses and city apartments, the radio carries his voice. For some families, it's the one place those names are said out loud.
The archbishop is Oscar Romero, and when he was chosen, some expected him to keep quiet.

teach.b: Romero was a careful, bookish priest when he was made archbishop, and some in power were glad of it.

teach.h: A FRIEND KILLED ON A COUNTRY ROAD.
teach.b: Soon after, his friend Rutilio Grande, a Jesuit who worked among poor farm families, was shot and killed on a country road, along with others traveling with him. Romero went to see the bodies.

Those who knew him say something changed in him that night. He began to speak: for farmers whose land and lives were taken, for families of the disappeared, for the poor his country had pushed to the edge.
He spoke against killing by any side. He used the pulpit and the radio, and when the church's radio station was bombed, he kept preaching.

teach.h: OPEN THY MOUTH FOR THE DUMB.
teach.b: Proverbs, in the King James Bible: "Open thy mouth for the dumb in the cause of all such as are appointed to destruction." Dumb there means unable to speak. People came to call Romero the voice of the voiceless.

On his last Sunday he spoke straight to the soldiers. Paraphrased: you are our brothers, and no soldier has to obey an order to kill that goes against the law of God. He begged them, in God's name, to stop the repression.
The next evening he was saying Mass in the hospital chapel where he lived, near cancer patients cared for by sisters.

As he finished his sermon and turned toward the altar, a gunman fired through the open chapel door. He fell at the altar. The Catholic Church has since named him a saint, and Christians beyond it remember him too.

how: The Catholic calendar marks Saint Oscar Romero's feast on the day of his death, and pilgrims visit the hospital chapel in San Salvador where he was killed.

games.q: you're the new archbishop. your friend, a priest who worked with poor farmers, has just been killed on a country road. what do you do?
o: stay quiet and keep the peace with those in power.
begin to speak, Sunday after Sunday, for the poor and the disappeared.
games.why: Romero began to speak, from the pulpit and on the radio, reading out names that no one else would say.

practice: Think of someone whose story doesn't get told: a worker nobody notices, a patient in a hallway, someone held somewhere, waiting.
Hold one of them in mind and say their situation to yourself plainly, as if you were reading it on the radio. If you pray, pray for them, by name if you know it.

wordCard.voice: Oscar Romero. An archbishop of San Salvador who spoke for the poor and the disappeared, and was shot while saying Mass.

orig.note: Hebrew, in Proverbs 31:8: the mute, one who cannot speak — the King James 'dumb'.

carryVoice: Your line: the voice of the voiceless. The week ran from a Birmingham cell to a hospital chapel, by way of a mountaintop, a little light, open windows, lifted sentences and Taizé. That's day nine hundred sixty-six.
